tagline: Working harbors and Fundy tides out to the easternmost light.
intro: The byway starts on US 1 at Milbridge, at the mouth of the Narraguagus River, and takes 147 miles to reach Calais. It is in no hurry. A loop runs out to Jonesport, a fishing and lobstering town. Past Machias, whose name roughly means "bad little falls" in Passamaquoddy, Route 191 heads out to Cutler and then along the coves toward Lubec.

Beyond Cutler harbor the coast comes under the tides of the Bay of Fundy, and the edge of the country is settled in fine print. Lubec is the easternmost town in the contiguous states, Eastport the easternmost city. The drive ends at Calais, at the head of tide on the St. Croix, across from Canada.

moments.title: Burnham Tavern, Machias
moments.text: Job Burnham's gambrel-roofed tavern of 1770, where the militia met before taking the Margaretta in June 1775, and where the wounded of both sides were afterward treated.

moments.title: West Quoddy Head Light
moments.text: A red-and-white striped brick tower of 1858 at the easternmost point of the contiguous states, though strictly the point is the rocks running east from the shore below it.

moments.title: Eastport
moments.text: Over the causeway onto Moose Island, an old sardine port with tides of about 25 feet, which the British took in 1814 and handed back in 1818.
